check3_outlier_treatment.note_about_ordering: The A/B/C variants use each channel's own metric after its own trimming, so a channel with a fatter tail can be trimmed harder. The common-union variants (a_common_5pct, b_common_single) remove the same observations for all three channels and are the fairer test; both keep the ordering.

extra_batch_leaveout.label_correction: in_db_row==True selects the 331 rows that DO have an exact database row (identical to in_reference_training_set True); in_db_row==False selects the 212 held-out rows.

threshold_trend.note: the claim 'the database covers only small molecules' is decided by the DB side, whose molecule count above the boundary is 0 for every threshold >= 10 and 70% of the DB for a threshold of 8; the benchmark side above the boundary falls monotonically from 234 obs (HAC>8) to 63 obs (HAC>12) but never reaches 0.

check5_threshold_sensitivity.verdict_note: DB HAC max is exactly 10 with 0 molecules above; benchmark observations above each threshold are reported; conclusion is threshold-insensitive in the sense that no DB molecule exceeds HAC 10 under any threshold >= 10, while the benchmark tail above the boundary shrinks monotonically with the threshold.

mean_vs_majority_reversal.interpretation: quantum wins on the MEAN absolute error but learned wins on the MAJORITY of individual observations; the mean advantage comes from quantum's thinner extreme tail, not from being better on a typical bond. Any claim phrased as 'quantum is the better estimator' must say which summary it refers to.

check2b_test_choice_sensitivity.verdict: PARTIAL - TEST-DEPENDENT. The mean-difference tests (paired t p=5.37e-05, row and cluster bootstrap CIs) and 4 of the 5 alternative loss metrics favour quantum. But the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p=0.553) and the within-2-kcal McNemar test (p=0.0784) do NOT reject, and the per-observation win count favours LEARNED (284 vs 246 observations, sign test p=0.108). There is a mean-vs-majority reversal: the mean gap is a tail-effect, not a typical-bond effect.

check4b_domain_split.verdict: the whole-sample 'quantum beats learned' result is carried by the 158 observations in HAC>=10|no_exact_db_row (diff -1.1311, CI [-1.6031, -0.6945]); in every other cell the difference is not distinguishable from 0 or points the other way, and on the 331 in-database rows quantum is if anything WORSE.

check_status.detail: max |dMAE| = 0.0515 kcal/mol over 419 leave-out fits (quantum 0.0252, learned 0.0421, reference 0.0515); channel order changed in 0/419 subsets; no single molecule drives the ranking.

quantum<learned<reference on MAE, RMSE, median AE, 90th-pct AE and fraction within 5 kcal/mol; only fraction-within-2 leaves q-vs-l undecided (CI -0.0018 to +0.0627). q-vs-r and l-vs-r significant on all five.

no ranking flip under own-5% trim, common-union-5% trim, own-single-worst, common-single-worst, or 1-99% winsorisation; q-vs-l mean gap shrinks from -0.313 to -0.137 (union 5%) / -0.289 (winsorised) but stays signed and CI-excludes-zero.

no BOND CLASS changes the ranking (drop C-C / C-H / H-O all keep quantum<learned<reference), but the SIZE/DATABASE batch does: dropping the HAC>=10 bin flips the order to learned (1.811) < quantum (1.829), and on the 331 in-database rows alone learned is better by 0.0639 kcal/mol. The q-vs-l headline is carried by 158 out-of-database, HAC>=10 observations.

coverage boundary holds at HAC 10/11/12 (0 DB molecules above) and the MW redefinition agrees (DB max MW 152.1, 138/543 benchmark observations above it); conclusion is direction-stable, magnitude threshold-dependent.

verdicts.claim: Reference channel is worse than both quantum and learned (MAE 5.49 vs 2.10/2.41)
verdicts.evidence: reference worst under every loss: MAE/RMSE/median/p90/pinball-free metrics; leave-one-molecule-out max |dMAE| for reference = 0.0515; no class removal changes the bottom rank; CI q-vs-r = [-3.7417688766114177, -3.05288950276243] and l-vs-r = [-3.4484019337016574, -2.718267955801105] both exclude 0.

verdicts.claim: Quantum beats learned on MAE (2.098 vs 2.411)
verdicts.evidence: mean |e| diff = -0.3129 kcal/mol, row CI [-0.4708,-0.1682], cluster CI [-0.4733, -0.1681], t p=5.37e-05 BUT Wilcoxon p=0.553. DECISIVE: the effect is carried entirely by the 158 observations in the HAC>=10 / parent-not-in-database cell (diff -1.131, CI [-1.6031, -0.6945]); on the 331 in-database rows the sign REVERSES (+0.0639 kcal/mol, CI [-0.0013, 0.1294]), and dropping the HAC 10+ bin flips the ranking to learned<quantum (learned MAE 1.811 vs quantum 1.829). Direction survives all 5 alternative losses and the unique-pair subset, but not the subset restriction.

verdicts.claim: Quantum and learned are NOT distinguishable (null result)
verdicts.evidence: REFUTED for the mean, SUPPORTED for the typical observation. The mean |e| difference is significantly nonzero (paired t p=5.4e-05; cluster bootstrap CI [-0.473, -0.168]), so 'not distinguishable' is false on the mean. But the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p=0.553), the within-2-kcal McNemar test (p=0.0784) and the per-observation win count all fail to favour quantum: LEARNED wins on 284 observations vs quantum's 246 (sign test p=0.108), and Cliffs delta is only -0.0417. So the channels ARE distinguishable on the mean (quantum better by 0.313 kcal/mol) but are NOT distinguishable / slightly reversed per typical bond - a mean-vs-majority reversal driven by quantum's thinner extreme tail (max |e| 15.7 vs learned's 25.2).

verdicts.claim: Database covers only small molecules (HAC<=10) while the benchmark extends larger
verdicts.evidence: DB HAC max = 10 exactly, over 42577 unique molecules; the count of DB molecules above the boundary is 29769 at HAC>8, 16373 at HAC>9 and 0 at HAC>10, >11 and >12 - so the DB-side boundary is hard, not a soft threshold artefact. Benchmark HAC max = 38 with 150 observations (27.6%) above 10 and 111 above 12; benchmark tail above the boundary declines monotonically (234/193/150/136/111 obs at cuts 8/9/10/11/12), so the SIZE of the uncovered region is threshold-sensitive but its EXISTENCE is not. MW check: DB max MW = 152.1; 138 benchmark observations (25.4%) exceed it, and benchmark HAC vs MW correlate at Spearman 0.9959, so the redefinition does not change the conclusion.

verdicts.claim: 331/543 observations have an exact database row; the remaining 212 do not
verdicts.evidence: exact-row matches = 331, unmatched = 212, parents present in DB = 369; reproduced identically from the raw join; all 212 unmatched rows are held-out (train_flag False) so this is one binary split, not two independent facts.

verdicts.claim: The quantum channel reproduces the database BDE on matched rows
verdicts.evidence: max |db-quantum| = 6.9985 kcal/mol; 30.2% within 0.01, 92.4% within 0.5; learned differs from the DB by up to 4.77 kcal/mol with only 5.1% within 0.01.

verdicts.claim: Bond class / size structure of the error (WS3-style class effects)
verdicts.evidence: the 543-observation benchmark contains only 3 labelled bond classes ({'C-H': np.int64(302), 'C-C': np.int64(240), 'H-O': np.int64(1)}); the H-O cell has n=1, so only C-H (n=302) and C-C (n=240) can be compared, and those two classes differ in size mix; the 9-class database taxonomy cannot be evaluated on this benchmark at all.

verdicts.claim: Database is exhaustive within its own domain
verdicts.evidence: 369 benchmark observations have a parent molecule in the DB and 331 of them have an exact fragment-pair row (89.7%); the two counts coincide, so no 'parent present but pair missing' case exists.

MAE on the 331 in-database rows vs the 212 held-out rows: quantum 1.871->2.452; learned 1.807->3.353; reference 5.024->6.207. Degradation is real for all three channels, but the q-vs-l ranking is REVERSED on the held-out subset: the subset orders are ['learned', 'quantum', 'reference'] (in-DB) and ['quantum', 'learned', 'reference'] (held-out), and the held-out q-vs-l difference is -0.9012 kcal/mol with CI [-1.2706, -0.5604] (includes 0). So the held-out claim is robust, but the 'quantum beats learned' claim does NOT hold out of database.

analysis_units.note: statistics over the 543 rows use bond observations; leave-one-molecule-out and the cluster bootstrap use the 419 molecules; check 6 uses fragment pairs. The three units are NOT interchangeable: q-vs-l is -0.313 on observations but -0.437 on one-row-per-molecule and -0.330 on unique fragment pairs.
